claim: With sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1) and P_4(t) denoting the assertion that for every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 4 with gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)>=t, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labels (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining labelled occurrences d^j, each pair used at most once and coincident numerical values retained separately, the threshold T_4=inf{t>=1:P_4(t)} equals 1.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 4 with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=b(m)=2+1/(m-1)+(floor(log_2(m))+1)/m, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labels (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining labelled occurrences d^j, each pair used at most once and coincident numerical values retained separately; moreover b(m)<=37/12 for every integer m>=4 and b(m) tends to 2 as m tends to infinity.
quadruple.stage: Finite labelled pure-power supplies in the nonnegative integers, their numerical finite-sum sets, probability measures on the discrete group Z and its characters.

shape.objects: Finite sets D of distinct integer bases and infinite locally finite labelled power supplies, with finite representing supports for individual integers; the target T_4 is a real infimum over sufficient reciprocal masses. Disjoint-support union and interval-plus-bounded-gap-reserve amplification are established operations, but a seed at every strictly-superunit mass is unknown. Finite label sets can support Bernoulli choices; no spread hypothesis is known. Core Lean/Mathlib has the elementary arithmetic objects, but a full library inventory for the new threshold and FS-mean definitions is unknown.
shape.quantifiers: The numerical claim T_4=1 concerns all thresholds above one and, in P_4(t), every finite gcd-one D of mass at least t, every positive cutoff k, every finite deletion F, then existence of N(D,k,F) and finite representations of every n>=N. Its strict-mass formulation is universally quantified over finite arithmetic inputs with existential finite supports; it is not a statement about all uncountable sets of reals. No uniform N over D,k,F is requested.
shape.target_quantity: The exact real threshold T_4, conjecturally1 and currently in[1,13/4], is the quantity to improve, not a yes/no proxy or an upper bound on the density of a configuration-avoiding set. Reciprocal mass1 is the necessary finite-base boundary recorded by Pomerance's converse. The mass bound must be explicit; unspecified auxiliary representation thresholds N(D,k,F) are acceptable and do not themselves settle the exact value of T_4.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer order, collective gcd, disjoint once-only label capacity, and harmonic-analysis structure coexist. The accepted amplification operation adjoins a represented interval on one supply to a bounded-gap finite-sum set on a disjoint reserve. Griesmer's Corollary4.2(ii) supplies a thickness theorem on Z given an extreme invariant mean and an FS-mean. A positive-density statement for an averaging supply is not needed by that theorem. A controlled probabilistic overlap parameter for arbitrary missing representations and a closed density-increment piece system remain unknown.
shape.symmetries: Base-label permutations and union of disjoint finite supports preserve numerical representation. Arbitrary mixed-base dilation, arbitrary translation, and intersection do not preserve the once-only pure-power support or its mass/gcd conditions. No general gluing across reused labels is allowed.
shape.configuration: The relation is n=sum_{(d,j) in H}d^j for one finite set H of legal labels, each used at most once, with distinct labels retained even at equal numerical values. It is not an avoidance configuration. Base restriction can destroy gcd or reciprocal mass, and truncation can destroy a proposed finite interval. A model dropping order or arithmetic does not carry this exact representation condition verbatim.
shape.finite_certificates: A represented finite interval plus an analytical disjoint reserve-gap bound is a checkable sufficient certificate for one D,k,F; individual finite label-subset calculations are checkable. No finite certificate or bounded search space for either side of the full T_4=1 statement is established. There is no reviewed finite computation, no global finite residue, and no known uniform maximum seed scale.
shape.monotonicity: P_4(t) weakens as the sufficient reciprocal threshold t increases. Its ideal boundary is1 and thresholds just above1 are open. Adding available labels or lowering a positive cutoff preserves representation. Individual cutoffs begin at one, but no finite maximum base or exponent is sufficient for this all-input claim.
shape.uniformity_parameter: No uniform auxiliary N is required over D,k,F, and no extra free optimisation parameter is the target. The difficulty selected here is reducing the sufficient reciprocal mass itself to its critical value1, not obtaining one N or one Bohr dimension uniformly over all inputs.
shape.proof_shape: Move2 gives an analytical b(m) rung candidate: full sequential Bernoulli FS-mean on a gcd-one supply, one disjoint mass-one density supply, one mass-one reserve, logarithmic gcd descent and strict first crossing. The partition criterion requires total mass strictly greater than two, so its reason cannot survive the exact target one. The native claim T_4=1 and strict below-b(m) remainder remain open. This is no universal FS-mean or completeness barrier.
shape.neighbours: Accepted local bounds are3+min{1/4,2/m} and separate ternary/common-radix families. The exact b(m) rung and the minimum-four strictly-superunit statement below it are open here; even the unrestricted m=4 strictly-superunit subclass remains open. The canonical original also includes minimum three and reciprocal equality. WOC, with no gcd restriction, is an open one-class piecewise-Bohr hypothesis, and its accepted implication reaches2+min{1/8,1/m}, not T_4=1. Known published analogues are the sum of two syndetic sets being piecewise Bohr and Griesmer's FS-mean plus positive-density sumset theorem. Abstract surplus and signed-tail versions have accepted counterexamples with checkable finite pieces. No incidence/rank/entropy translation of this exact claim, verbatim simpler ambient, property-reflecting categorical correspondence, or countable/uncountable independence contrast is established.
shape.known_bounds: Accepted bounds remain 1<=T_4<=13/4 until exact independent review. Move2 supplies an unconditional analytical candidate at b(m)=2+1/(m-1)+(floor(log_2(m))+1)/m, with b(m)<=37/12 and b(m)->2, pending acceptance. Its exact disjoint-base criterion cannot apply to total mass at most two. No all-input strictly-superunit theorem, WOC theorem or counterexample to the original objective is claimed.
shape.missing_input: The exact open local remainder is all-cutoff/deletion representation for minimum-four finite gcd-one inputs with 1<sigma(D)<b(min D). The new disjoint two-mass-one-supply criterion has no inputs at total mass at most two. A new mechanism must avoid that simultaneous disjoint-base mass requirement; scalar normalization, generic surplus and common-radix alone do not supply it.
shape.base_theory: Ordinary classical mathematics with choice, including standard compactness of means and the cited harmonic-analysis theorem. The original finite-base problem and all stated hypotheses are inside this theory, not extra set-theoretic axioms. No independence, forcing or guessing principle is asserted. A future formal interface check could use Lean's standard axioms, but would require exact library, declaration and controlled-execution audits before any claim of machine verification.
